title: 3 · Core Code: Stable Kernel, Evolvable Harness
purpose: Show a model-portable agent runtime in which versioned vertical profiles and evolvable harness modules communicate through a stable semantic ABI, every real-world effect and durable event remains under a small Effect Kernel, and governed evidence can change the active runtime only through conformance, independent evaluation, canary, signed release, registry activation, and named rollback.
caption: Freeze authority. Evolve policy. Keep every model replaceable.

forbidden_edges.reason: Observe may read governed evidence but cannot update a profile before evaluation and signed release.
A HarnessPatch is an isolated candidate; Propose cannot mutate the running harness.
Evaluation cannot activate a candidate without canary, signed release, and registry activation.
Canary success still requires a signed release tuple and registry activation.
Every release must enter the Runtime Registry before activation.
Models and physical model adapters never invoke real tools or environments directly.
Execution IR emits typed intents and proposals; only the Effect Kernel owns invocation.
ToolIntent and EffectProposal are not effect authority.
No learned module may bypass capability checks and effect commit.
Model output must be decoded into Execution IR and stable ABI contracts before reaching the kernel.
Harness modules must communicate through the stable semantic ABI.
External results and receipts must return through the Effect Kernel.
Models cannot write durable evidence directly; Event Commit belongs to the Effect Kernel.
Learned modules cannot append or rewrite durable evidence outside kernel event commit.
Optimizer proposals require governed observation and diagnosis, not direct raw-log access.
Raw private traces cannot enter training without governance, residualization, curation, and permission checks.
New weights must pass runtime recalibration, conformance, evaluation, canary, and signed release.
An unreleased model candidate cannot become active.
Rollback selects an existing known-good tuple; it does not mint a new release.

layout_notes: Use a layered central stack: versioned profiles and evolvable harness at the top; the narrow Stable Semantic ABI above Canonical Execution IR; the Effect Kernel and Append-Only Event Log centered on the trust boundary; model portability and sandboxed environments below.
Place the optional post-training chain on the far left and the constrained optimizer, release, registry, active version, and rollback path on the far right.
Draw CC-03/CC-04, CC-05/CC-06, CC-07/CC-08, CC-09/CC-10, CC-13/CC-14, and CC-15/CC-16 in visibly separate request and response lanes; never merge a pair into one line.
Make CC-15 APPEND the primary event direction and CC-16 REPLAY a separate dashed reverse lane with no visual suggestion that replay re-executes an external effect.
Route CC-17 from the Event Log to Observe through a visibly governed read corridor; it must not resemble direct optimizer write access to the log.
Reserve one outer perimeter lane for evaluation failure back to Diagnose, canary or production failure to Guarded Rollback, and Guarded Rollback to the named registry target.
Show Hard Constraints as an independent authority feeding both the Effect Kernel and Independent Evaluate, never as an optimizer-owned module.
Keep Stable Semantic ABI, Effect Kernel, Append-Only Event Log, Hard Constraints, evaluator integrity, and registry authority visibly outside the optimizer search surface.
Show the Model + Physical Adapter Matrix as replaceable candidates; only a registry-pinned pair that passed Model Conformance Gate may be selected by the active runtime.
Use braces, bands, or inset text for component inventories and ownership; do not invent arrows between contained items.
required_text: Harness: Context · Memory · Tool Surface · Model Router · Topology · Scheduler · Verifier · Recovery · Escalation
ABI: TaskEnvelope · ContextRequest · ToolIntent · EffectProposal · ArtifactRef
Kernel: Identity · Capability Check · Event Commit · Effect Commit · Version Registry · Kill / Rollback
Adapters: Patch · Replace · JSON / Function Call · Token Protocol
Models: Open A · Open B · Frontier · Local
Release Tuple: model_id + runtime_id + adapter_id + context_snapshot + policy_id + eval_suite_id
Rollback Target: previous known-good signed tuple
No model or learned module bypasses the Effect Kernel.
Training is optional. Evaluation is mandatory.
